cells.tense: You are reading the field right now, and you are holding the pen.
cells.act: return the small thing you owe before anyone asks
cells.ask: Settle that small debt you have been carrying quietly. Do it before anyone has to mention it, and say nothing about it after.
cells.core:
You can look over what has come in and know what's fair without getting tangled in it. The harvest is here — what you waited on has grown — and your own sense of what is right in it moves cleanly. You add what should be added, subtract what shouldn't, and what passes between you and other people balances without a ledger.

Settle one open account. Small, before anyone has to mention it, no accounting afterward. The private compass knows the case; it just hasn't been acted on. Doing it is the adjustment. Afterward the next case will be easier to see, and the one past it won't need weighing — the balance holds because you moved.
cells.sheetLine: Your own sense of what is fair is working. Settle the small thing.
cells.verb: reading the field for what it has already grown
cells.place: a season of weighing what has come in

cells.tense: You will be reading the field before it has finished, and you know it.
cells.act: spend an hour with the thing you love without a task attached to it
cells.ask: Give something you love an hour with nothing attached — no task, no purpose, no one to report to. Let that be the whole of it.
cells.core:
You're already measuring what has not come in, and the measuring has gotten past the season. The field gets read for yield before the yield is fully here, and each reading wants the next one. That is not patience; that is bracing against a future you cannot write in.

Spend an hour with something you love and attach nothing to it. No purpose, no report, no next step. The feeling already knows what it knows; let it settle into its own depth without pulling a lesson out of it. Nothing about what is growing needs a decision from you. The connection is whole without your assessment of it.

cells.tense: You were reading the field once, and you are still standing at a door behind you.
cells.act: move at the pace your feeling can sustain
cells.ask: Take the next small piece of what you tend, and do it at a pace you could keep for a month. Let the pace itself be the point.
cells.core:
You aren't looking at what has come in. The door you stood at is behind you, and the present field has not been read. The waiting got so patient it stopped arriving. The pull that used to carry you forward is not carrying you now — the work goes on, but the direction has thinned.

Take the next piece at a pace your feeling can hold for a month, not the pace of a single day. Nothing needs forcing into it. That rhythm returns through the body before it returns through the will. Feeling and direction move together once you stop holding them apart. Let the steady work be the arrival, even without a harvest to show yet.
cells.sheetLine: The waiting went past arriving. Move at the pace you can hold.

cells.tense: You are reading the field right now, and someone else has been given the pen.
cells.act: declare the shape of it outward, plainly
cells.ask: When the right arrangement of something is clear to you, say it plainly before anyone asks. Don't cushion it. State it once and move on.
cells.core:
Something in you is already reading the field — knowing what's fair, knowing what should be kept and what released — and the reading gets filed under circumstance. The calls are yours, but the season has its name on them.

When the right arrangement of something is clear, say it openly before anyone asks. Don't argue for it, don't cushion it. State it once and move on. Structure serves what it organizes; it does not need a defense. Speaking it in the open returns the pen to the hand that has been writing with it anyway. The accuracy was the part that was not in question.

attempts.check: The record supports 'watching what it produced' as the capacity of Harvest in Tune, but I am choosing to render the work of this seat as 'reading the field for what it already yields' — that is a reading, not a fact, and the person could reasonably say 'no, that's not what I'm doing, I'm still waiting.' The ask still works if my read is wrong: the act of reading yield is still usable even if the person is not yet in a gathering season. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'the work of this seat is reading, not reaping' — I cut it before writing the cells. Fixed by narrowing the claims to what the person can recognise in a moment and placing the ask on the medicine's own act.
